- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33) over 3–5 days, model underestimates prices; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect bearish sentiment reversal.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.2–0.8% bias to early periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mid-term prices when sentiment is volatile; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment if sentiment swings >2x in last 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
